subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` config contract, and should `enabled: false` remove that provider from all model generation, catalog, fallback, status, and probe paths while preserving its config?
rationale: Root policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces, and current code has several provider-routing surfaces that must share one intentional disabled-provider semantic.

options.title: Approve narrow provider disable contract
options.body: Add the documented optional flag with default-enabled behavior and require every provider-resolution/status surface to honor it consistently.

options.title: Defer to broader provider UX
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers design a larger provider enable/disable and status workflow instead of adding a standalone config key.

options.title: Decline new config surface
options.body: Close the direction and document the supported workaround of removing or regenerating provider config when a provider must be taken out of service.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow provider disable contract
recommendation.body: Add the documented optional flag with default-enabled behavior and require every provider-resolution/status surface to honor it consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across model selection, models-config planning, and models status, and already reviewed this issue as still active.
